column1: What is the foundational architectural invariant that distinguishes a PLC from a general-purpose computer running a preemptive multitasking OS?
column2: Bounded, deterministic real-time operation via a single monolithic scan cycle with guaranteed worst-case execution time, eliminating context-switching overhead and priority inversion hazards.

column1: Describe the three-phase PLC scan cycle model and its causality implication.
column2: Input acquisition (sample inputs into input image table) → logic solve (execute ladder logic against frozen snapshot) → output update (write to output image table). This guarantees an input transition cannot affect outputs until the next scan cycle, creating a minimum propagation delay equal to one full scan time.

column1: In PLC I/O module design, what is the purpose of optoisolator circuits on discrete input modules?
column2: To provide galvanic isolation (e.g., 2500VAC) between field-side electrical signals and the PLC's internal logic circuitry, protecting the CPU from voltage spikes and noise while converting signals (e.g., 24VDC) to logic-level pulses.

column1: What year was the Modicon 084 introduced, and why is it historically significant?
column2: 1969. It was Richard Morley's solid-state replacement for hardwired relay panels, encoding relay logic semantics into semiconductor memory and executing them via a deterministic scan cycle, establishing the PLC paradigm.

column1: What year was IEC 61131-3 ratified, and what core problem did it solve?
column2: 1993. It unified five PLC programming languages under a common type system, execution model, and program organization hierarchy, eliminating vendor lock-in and incompatible proprietary ladder logic semantics across manufacturers.

column1: List the IEC 61131-3 containment hierarchy from largest to smallest scope.
column2: Configuration → Resource → Task → Program → Program Organization Unit (POU). Configuration = entire control system; Resource = individual processing unit; Task = real-time scheduling quantum; Program = namespace of control logic.

column1: Why does IEC 61131-3 prohibit implicit type coercion (e.g., REAL to INT)?
column2: Because silent rounding errors in analog signal processing or flow rate calculations could trigger catastrophic failures in safety-critical systems like chemical reactors or hydraulic presses; explicit conversion functions are required instead.

column1: What are the five IEC 61131-3 programming languages?
column2: Ladder Diagram (LD), Function Block Diagram (FBD), Structured Text (ST), Instruction List (IL), and Sequential Function Chart (SFC).

column1: What is the fundamental invariant governing the division of responsibility in SCADA architecture?
column2: Unidirectional flow of control responsibility (downward) and bidirectional flow of information: field devices (PLCs/RTUs) retain ultimate real-time control authority and continue local operation during communication failures, while SCADA exercises only supervisory authority (setpoints, commands) and receives continuous upward telemetry.

column1: Why can't SCADA systems perform fast closed-loop control (e.g., a 100ms temperature loop) over wide-area networks?
column2: Because communication latencies (tens of ms on local Ethernet up to seconds over cellular/satellite) can exceed the required loop response time, causing instability; so time-critical control is delegated to local field intelligence instead.

column1: In Modbus, what are the four data structure types a slave device address space contains?
column2: Coils (discrete outputs), Discrete Inputs (read-only bits), Holding Registers (16-bit read-write words), and Input Registers (16-bit read-only words).

column1: What is the standard RS-485 termination resistor value and why is it required?
column2: 120 Ω, matching the characteristic impedance of twisted-pair cable, to prevent signal reflections that would corrupt the differential voltage and disrupt deterministic bus communication.
